findings.evidence: Resolving.lean:87 `ExactK0.ofLEEquiv fun _ => by rw [GradedExactStructure.fullSubcategory_toExactStructure]` vs Resolution.lean:88 `ExactK0.ofLEEquiv fun _ => by rw [fullSubcategory_toExactStructure]`; Resolving.lean:107-109 vs Resolution.lean:106-108 (`induction r with | base hX => simp | step … => simp [ih]`) are identical.
findings.fix: Move the `Transport` section of `Laurent/Resolution.lean` into a shared module (e.g. `Laurent/Transport.lean`, importing `Exact.Graded.FullSubcategory`, `Laurent.Basic`, `GrothendieckGroup.Resolution`), drop `private`, import it from both files and delete lines 84-109 here. The hypotheses of that section (`LocallySmall`, `EssentiallySmall R`, `R.ContainsZero`, `R.IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts`, `hR`, `hRshift`) are all available here from `[E.toExactStructure.IsResolving P]`, `[EssentiallySmall.{w} C]` and the local instance at line 73.
findings.issue: `toUngraded`, `toUngraded_of`, `toUngraded_symm_of` and `ofExactK0_toUngraded_symm_eulerClassFullSubcategory` (lines 84-109) are verbatim copies of the `private` declarations at `Laurent/Resolution.lean:85-108`, duplicated only because those are private. `E.toExactStructure.resolvingSubcategory P` is the `abbrev` `E.fullSubcategory P IsResolving.isExtensionClosed` (`Exact/Resolving.lean:96-97`), so the new `toUngraded` is the old one at `R := P`, `hR := hP`, with the same proof.

findings.evidence: Resolving.lean:142-143 `map_smul' c x := by simp only [AddEquiv.toFun_eq_coe, resolutionAddEquiv_apply, map_smul, RingHom.id_apply]` equals Resolution.lean:163-164 verbatim; `laurentResolutionEquiv_apply := (rfl)` and `laurentResolutionEquiv_toLinearMap := LinearMap.ext …` likewise match Resolution.lean:166-176. No such helper exists in `Laurent/Basic.lean` (grepped the file).
findings.fix: Add a constructor in `Laurent/Basic.lean`, e.g. `noncomputable def LaurentK0.linearEquivOfMap (h : GradedConflationExact E E' F) (e : LaurentK0 E ≃+ LaurentK0 E') (he : ∀ x, e x = map h x) : LaurentK0 E ≃ₗ[LaurentPolynomial ℤ] LaurentK0 E'` with a `@[simp]` `toLinearMap` lemma, and have both this file and `Laurent/Resolution.lean` supply only `he`.
findings.issue: The argument upgrading an additive equivalence to a `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`-linear one — `resolutionAddEquiv_apply` via `ExactK0.hom_ext` + `DFunLike.congr_fun`, then `map_smul'` by `simp only [AddEquiv.toFun_eq_coe, …, map_smul, RingHom.id_apply]`, then `_apply := (rfl)` and `_toLinearMap := LinearMap.ext …` (lines 112-155) — is the second verbatim instance of `Laurent/Resolution.lean:136-176`. The reusable fact (an `AddEquiv` agreeing pointwise with `LaurentK0.map h` is `q`-linear) stays hidden in both files.

summary: Proofs are short and free of defeq manipulation, but the module re-proves two blocks verbatim from Laurent/Resolution.lean instead of reusing them: the four transport declarations and the AddEquiv-to-Laurent-linear upgrade. Both should be factored into a shared, non-private module.
